task: Extract a single shared customer-config component resolution (YAML + runtime + dynamic override) used by both the backend flag reads and GET /v1/config, with a TTL-bounded override snapshot warmed and refreshed at API startup.

component_scope.label: L
component_scope.affected: configs.component_resolution (new shared module), configs.customer_config (CustomerConfig singleton + Component/ComponentSetting re-export), service.customer_config_service (OverrideCache, refresh_overrides, resolve_components, list_settings), service.customer_config_declarations, rest_api.main (startup warm-up + background refresh task)
component_scope.layers: Config/Infra, Service, API (startup lifespan), Agent-Tool (toolkit flag reads consume the snapshot)

requirements_clarity.label: M
requirements_clarity.gaps: The ticket asserted is_feature_enabled defaults to True for unknown keys while the code and an existing test both say False; settled with the user before implementation and resolved by correcting a wrong docstring only. One planned item (surfacing CUSTOMER_CONFIG_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS in .env.example) was attempted and reverted because a test pins that file to an exact key list.

technical_risk.label: L
technical_risk.risk_factors: No exact precedent for per-field override merge semantics; module-level mutable snapshot published from the async side and read synchronously by request-path flag reads; TTL cache with degradation fallbacks (last-good snapshot, then YAML); markup sanitisation path (bleach + dangerous-scheme rejection) in the write path; a real regression was introduced and caught in review — folding the declaration's neutral defaults into every stored override overwrote YAML values and disabled releaseNotesRecentCount outright, because its declaration carries no `enabled` field while YAML sets enabled: true
technical_risk.mitigation: One code-review round fixed 1 critical and 5 major findings; apply_override now lays only the override's own fields over YAML; no schema change and no call-site changes, so rollback is a plain revert

key_reasoning.reason: 13 files changed across 6 directories, 6 of them new — 715 insertions / 112 deletions. The new module plus five new test files dominate; only 4 production files were edited.

A core shared utility was restructured: Component/ComponentSetting moved into the new component_resolution module and had to be re-exported from configs.customer_config because five modules import them from there (three of them tests that had to keep passing unchanged). This relocation was not in the initial plan.

The predicted risk materialised — code review found 1 critical and 5 major issues, all fixed in one round. The critical one was a self-inflicted regression in the override merge that silently disabled a live feature, exactly the blast radius a shared resolver carries.
The ticket contradicted the code on the unknown-key default; settled with the user up front, so the contradiction cost a docstring rather than rework.

Three layers only — config, service and API startup. No schema migration (the existing dynamic_config table was reused), no external calls, and none of the 21 flag read sites changed, which held the layer count down.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from M (3) to L (4): touches a core shared utility — the customer_config singleton read from 21 flag call sites, whose model classes had to move and be re-exported
Requirements Clarity bumped from S (2) to M (3): conflicting requirement — the ticket's stated default for unknown feature keys contradicted both the code and an existing test
